version.changelog: Simplify install section, remove brew metadata

llm.summary: The skill is internally coherent: it uses the hf CLI and a Hugging Face token (HF_TOKEN) as expected for managing Hub resources, but the token's scope grants potentially destructive powers so the user should be careful which token they provide.

dimensions.detail: The declared requirements (hf binary, HF_TOKEN) match the skill's stated purpose of managing Hugging Face repos, models, datasets, spaces, jobs, endpoints, etc. No unrelated binaries or credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells the agent to run many hf commands including destructive actions (repos delete, buckets delete, endpoints delete, jobs run/cancel) and to read/sync local directories. This is expected for a CLI wrapper, but it means the agent — when invoked — can perform deletions, uploads, and billing-impacting cloud jobs if given a write-scoped token.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec in the registry (instruction-only). The document recommends installing via curl -LsSf https://hf.co/cli/install.sh | bash. That URL is the official hf.co short domain, which is reasonable, but piping remote scripts to a shell is inherently higher risk than using a vetted package manager; users should verify the source before running.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only HF_TOKEN is required and it is the expected credential for the hf CLI. However, HF_TOKEN can be issued with 'write' scope that allows repo/bucket deletion, uploads, endpoint deployment, and running cloud jobs — granting significant privileges. The SKILL.md explicitly describes read vs write scopes and when write is required.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not set to always: true and does not request persistent system privileges. It does instruct how users might persist HF_TOKEN in their shell profile (a user action), but the skill itself does not alter other skills or system-wide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent for managing Hugging Face via the official CLI, but be careful with the token you provide: prefer a read-scoped HF_TOKEN if you only need browsing or downloads. If you must grant write access, create a token limited to the minimal required permissions and consider using a separate token for destructive or deploy operations. Verify the hf CLI installer (https://hf.co/cli/install.sh) is from the official source before running a curl | bash install. Remember that invoking this skill (or allowing the agent to invoke it) can run commands that delete repos/buckets, upload data, and start cloud jobs that may incur costs — only enable the skill and provide tokens you trust.
